subQuestions.questionText: A bucket rests on a table. What is the reaction force to the WEIGHT of the bucket according to Newton's Third Law?

options.A: Normal force of table on bucket
options.B: Force of bucket on Earth (gravitational pull of bucket on Earth)
options.C: Weight of table on the ground
options.D: Normal force of bucket on table

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The weight of the bucket is the gravitational pull of the Earth on the bucket. Its Newton's 3rd law pair is the gravitational pull of the bucket on the Earth.

subQuestions.questionText: A ball falls freely from rest. Which ONE of the following statements about the KINETIC ENERGY (Ek) and MOMENTUM (p) of the ball is CORRECT?

options.A: Both Ek and p remain constant.
options.C: Ek changes but p remains constant.
options.D: p changes but Ek remains constant.

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
As the ball accelerates, both its velocity and momentum increase. Kinetic energy also increases. Both change.

subQuestions.questionText: A ball is dropped from a height h and its momentum just before it hits the ground is p. The ball is now dropped from a height of 2h. What is the momentum of the ball just before hitting the ground?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
v = √(2gh). From 2h: v' = √(2g·2h) = √2·v. p' = mv' = m√2·v = √2·p.

subQuestions.questionText: The gravitational force between two objects is F. The distance between the objects is DOUBLED. What is the new gravitational force?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
F ∝ 1/r². If r doubles, F' = F/4 = ¼F.

subQuestions.questionText: An object is moved along two different paths between two points. The same amount of work is done along both paths. Which type of force is responsible?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
A conservative force (such as gravity) does work independent of path taken. The gravitational force is conservative.

subQuestions.questionText: A star is moving towards Earth. How would this star's light appear when observed from Earth?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
A source moving towards the observer causes blue shift — the observed wavelength decreases (shorter) / frequency increases.

subQuestions.questionText: Two opposite charges are released from rest and move towards each other. Which ONE of the following best describes the ACCELERATION of each charge as they approach?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
As opposites attract and move closer, r decreases. F = kq₁q₂/r² increases. Therefore acceleration a = F/m increases.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following CORRECTLY defines the EMF of a cell?

options.A: The total energy per unit charge dissipated in the external circuit
options.B: The potential difference across the terminals when current flows
options.C: The maximum potential difference across the internal resistance
options.D: The maximum energy per unit charge supplied by the cell

subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
EMF = maximum energy (work done) per unit charge by the cell = total energy transferred per coulomb through the cell.

subQuestions.questionText:
An AC generator produces a peak voltage of 100 V at frequency f. The speed of rotation is DOUBLED. What is the new peak voltage and the time for one rotation?

*(Refer to the circuit/generator data in the original question paper.)*
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Doubling speed doubles frequency (T halves → T' = 0.02 s) and doubles peak EMF (V_max doubles → 200 V).

subQuestions.questionText: A photon has energy 2X joules. The work function of the metal is X joules. What is the MAXIMUM KINETIC ENERGY of the ejected photoelectron?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Ek(max) = E_photon − W = 2X − X = X J.

subQuestions.questionText: State NEWTON'S FIRST LAW of motion in words.
subQuestions.memoText: An object will remain in its state of rest or motion at constant velocity unless a non-zero net force acts on it. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A man (70 kg) is attached to a tube (4 kg) and is being lifted by a helicopter at CONSTANT SPEED. A rope connects the man-tube system at 50° to the vertical. Friction on the tube = 300 N upward. Draw a FREE-BODY DIAGRAM for the man-tube system.
subQuestions.memoText: Forces: Weight of system (74 × 9.8 = 725.2 N downward), Tension T (along rope at 50°), Friction (300 N upward). All labelled correctly. (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the TENSION in the rope.
subQuestions.memoText: At constant speed, Fnet = 0. Vertical: T cos50° + 300 = 725.2 → T cos50° = 425.2 → T = 425.2/cos50° = 661.3 N. (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The helicopter now accelerates upward. What effect does this have on the tension? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: Tension INCREASES. When accelerating upward, Fnet is upward so T must increase to provide net force upward in addition to supporting the weight. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The tube is released and sinks 0.8 m into the water from a speed of 16 m/s. Calculate the AVERAGE UPWARD FORCE on the tube while sinking.
subQuestions.memoText: v² = v₀² + 2aΔx: 0 = 16² + 2a(0.8) → a = −160 m/s². Net force = ma = 4 × (−160) = −640 N (downward). F_net = F_up − mg. F_up = mg + 640 wait: F_up − mg = ma_net. Taking up positive: F_up − (4×9.8) = 4×160 (deceleration means a = −160 but net force upward). F_up = 4×160 + 4×9.8 = 640 + 39.2 = 679.2 N. (5 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term PROJECTILE.
subQuestions.memoText: A projectile is an object that moves under the influence of gravity only (no other forces). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Disc C is thrown from the top of a 30 m building at 15 m/s upward. Calculate the TIME for C to reach maximum height.
subQuestions.memoText: At max height, v = 0. v = v₀ − gt: 0 = 15 − 9.8t → t = 15/9.8 = 1.53 s. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the MAXIMUM HEIGHT of disc C above the GROUND.
subQuestions.memoText: Height above roof: Δy = v₀t − ½gt² = 15(1.53) − ½(9.8)(1.53²) = 22.95 − 11.48 = 11.47 m. Max height above ground = 30 + 11.47 = 41.47 m ≈ 41.5 m. (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Ball B is projected upward from the ground at 40 m/s, 0.5 s AFTER disc C is thrown. Calculate the TIME (after B is projected) until B hits C.
subQuestions.memoText: Position of C (taking ground = 0, upward positive): y_C = 30 + 15(t+0.5) − ½(9.8)(t+0.5)². Position of B: y_B = 40t − ½(9.8)t². Set equal and solve for t. (6 marks — simultaneous equation solution.)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw VELOCITY-TIME GRAPHS for both disc C and ball B on the same set of axes, from the moment C is thrown until B hits C.
subQuestions.memoText: C: starts at +15 m/s, decreases linearly to 0 then continues to negative. B: starts 0.5 s later at +40 m/s, decreasing linearly. Both straight lines with same gradient (−g). Time axes labelled. (5 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term ISOLATED SYSTEM (in the context of momentum).
subQuestions.memoText: A system on which the resultant external force is zero / a system that has no net external force acting on it. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A rocket is mounted on a cart (total 20 kg) moving at 2.5 m/s. The rocket is fired at 30 m/s and the cart slows to 0.6 m/s. Using physics principles, EXPLAIN why the cart slows down.
subQuestions.memoText: By Newton's 3rd Law, the rocket exerts a backward force on the cart. By Newton's 2nd Law this force causes a backward acceleration, slowing the cart. Momentum is conserved (isolated system). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the MASS of the rocket.
subQuestions.memoText: p_before = 20 × 2.5 = 50 kg·m/s. Let mass of rocket = m, cart mass = (20 − m). p_after = m × 30 + (20 − m) × 0.6. Conservation: 50 = 30m + 12 − 0.6m = 29.4m + 12. 29.4m = 38. m = 38/29.4 = 1.29 kg. (5 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State the WORK-ENERGY THEOREM.
subQuestions.memoText: The net work done on an object equals the change in kinetic energy of the object. W_net = ΔEk. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A 30 000 kg truck moving at 33 m/s enters an ascending arrester bed at 28°. State why the NET WORK done on the truck is NEGATIVE.
subQuestions.memoText: The truck decelerates (slows down), so its kinetic energy decreases. By the work-energy theorem, the net work is negative. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the MINIMUM LENGTH of the ascending arrester bed (friction = 31 000 N, incline 28°) needed to stop the truck.
subQuestions.memoText: W_net = ΔEk: (−f − mg sin28°)d = 0 − ½mv². (−31000 − 30000×9.8×sin28°)d = −½×30000×33². Solve for d. (5 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Would the truck stop in a SHORTER or LONGER distance if it enters the arrester bed going DOWNHILL (instead of uphill)? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: LONGER distance. Going downhill, gravity has a component along the direction of motion (adding to kinetic energy / reducing net braking force). Both friction AND gravity component down oppose stopping, so the bed must be longer. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State the DOPPLER EFFECT.
subQuestions.memoText: The Doppler effect is the apparent change in frequency (or pitch) of a wave when the source and observer are in relative motion. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A stationary source emits sound at 880 Hz. Calculate the WAVELENGTH of the sound emitted by the source (speed of sound = 340 m/s).
A car moves at 10 m/s TOWARDS the stationary source (880 Hz). Detector A is on the car. Calculate the frequency detected by A.
Detector B is on the stationary source. SKETCH a graph showing the frequency detected by B as the car approaches and then passes.
subQuestions.memoText: Sketch: constant frequency = 880 Hz (B is stationary, car moves — source is stationary so detector B hears the source frequency unchanged at 880 Hz regardless of car motion). (2 marks) Note: Detector B is ON the source — source is stationary and B is not moving relative to the source. B detects emitted frequency = 880 Hz throughout.

subQuestions.questionText: State COULOMB'S LAW in words.
subQuestions.memoText: The electrostatic force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw the ELECTRIC FIELD PATTERN for charges P (+3 × 10⁻⁶ C) and T (−3 × 10⁻⁶ C) placed 0.1 m apart.
subQuestions.memoText: Field lines: radially outward from P, radially inward toward T. Lines connect P to T. Lines are smooth and never cross. Minimum 8 lines shown symmetrically. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A third charge S is placed such that the net force on S is 10 N directed towards T. What is the SIGN of charge S?
subQuestions.memoText: S is NEGATIVE. The net force on S is towards T (+charge). Attraction means S is negative, repulsion from P (also positive) would push S away from P. The net 10 N direction confirms S is negative. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the NUMBER OF ELECTRONS that must be added to (or removed from) a neutral sphere to give it charge Q_S, if the net force on S is 10 N. (S is 0.15 m from T.)
subQuestions.memoText: F_TS = kQ_T × Q_S / r_TS² → find Q_S. Also F_PS on S and vector addition gives net 10 N. Full vector calculation needed. n = Q_S / e = Q_S / 1.6×10⁻¹⁹. (6 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A graph of E vs 1/r² is plotted for a charged sphere A. What does this graph show about the relationship between E and 1/r²?
subQuestions.memoText: E is directly proportional to 1/r² (linear graph through origin). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The gradient of the E vs 1/r² graph for sphere A is 680 N·m²/C. Calculate the ELECTRIC FIELD E at a given point using this gradient.
subQuestions.memoText: E = gradient × (1/r²) = kQ. Q = gradient/k = 680/(9×10⁹) = 7.56×10⁻⁸ C. E = kQ/r² = 680/r². (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The gradient of sphere B's E vs 1/r² graph is GREATER than that of A. Compare the CHARGE on B vs A. Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: Charge on B is GREATER than on A. Gradient = kQ. Greater gradient → greater kQ → greater Q. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Define an OHMIC CONDUCTOR.
subQuestions.memoText: An ohmic conductor is one that obeys Ohm's law — the ratio of voltage to current (resistance) remains constant at constant temperature. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: When switch S is OPEN, voltmeter V₁ reads 3.2 V. The battery has r = 0.5 Ω. Calculate the current when S is open.
subQuestions.memoText: When S is open: only resistor branch (4 Ω) is active. V = IR: I = V/R = 3.2/4 = 0.8 A. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the EMF of the battery.
When S is closed, voltmeter V₂ reads 8.8 V. The circuit has 4 Ω and 8 Ω in parallel and a series resistor R. Calculate the RESISTANCE of R.
subQuestions.memoText: V₂ = 8.8 V (terminal voltage when S closed). I_total = (emf − V₂)/r. R_parallel(4Ω ∥ 8Ω) = 4×8/(4+8) = 2.67 Ω. V_parallel = I×R_parallel. V_R = V₂ − V_parallel. R = V_R/I. (5 marks — full circuit calculation.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the BATTERY HEATS UP during operation.
subQuestions.memoText: Current flows through the internal resistance r of the battery. Energy is dissipated as heat in the internal resistance (P = I²r). The battery has resistance and resists current flow, producing thermal energy. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State the ENERGY CONVERSION that takes place in a DC motor.
subQuestions.memoText: Electrical energy is converted to mechanical (kinetic) energy. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Does a DC motor use AC or DC current?
subQuestions.memoText: DC (direct current). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State the FUNCTION of the commutator in a DC motor.
subQuestions.memoText: The commutator reverses the direction of current in the coil every half rotation to ensure continuous rotation in one direction. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Resistor Y is rated 220 V, 100 W. Calculate the RESISTANCE of Y.
subQuestions.memoText: P = V²/R → R = V²/P = 220²/100 = 484 Ω. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: When resistor X is added in series with Y, the power of Y changes to 80 W. The AC supply is 220 V rms. Calculate the POWER RATING X of resistor Z.
Define the PHOTOELECTRIC EFFECT.
subQuestions.memoText: The photoelectric effect is the process whereby electrons are ejected from the surface of a metal when electromagnetic radiation of sufficient frequency (above the threshold frequency) shines on it. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Light of frequency 1.2 × 10¹⁵ Hz shines on a metal plate. The total energy absorbed by the metal per second is 1.75 × 10⁻⁹ J. Calculate the NUMBER OF PHOTOELECTRONS ejected per second.
subQuestions.memoText: Energy per photon: E = hf = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 1.2×10¹⁵ = 7.956×10⁻¹⁹ J. Number per second = Total energy / E_photon = 1.75×10⁻⁹ / 7.956×10⁻¹⁹ = 2.2 × 10⁹ photons/s. Since one photon ejects one electron (if above W), n = 2.2 × 10⁹ per second. (4 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the MAXIMUM SPEED of photoelectrons ejected. The threshold frequency f₀ = 9.09 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
Explain how an EMISSION SPECTRUM is formed.
subQuestions.memoText: When electrons in excited atoms drop from higher to lower energy levels, they emit photons with specific energies (E = hf). Each transition produces a photon of specific frequency, resulting in a series of bright lines at specific frequencies — the emission spectrum. (2 marks)
